builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: BISECT: Bilevel Spectral Decomposition for Low-Rank Continual Learning
summary: BISECT replaces null-space-projected (subspace-isolated) LoRA updates in exemplar-free continual learning by splitting a fixed rank-r budget into an invariant carrier from dominant joint Gram-matrix modes and a whitened novelty complement, then folding both into the frozen backbone via a closed-form precision gate. It costs nothing at inference (no extra parameters or FLOPs) and fits a single 24 GB GPU, but adds training-time complexity: Gram-matrix estimation, generalized Rayleigh whitening, and per-task spectral decomposition. It can fail if the spectral-starvation diagnosis does not transfer to the reader's domain, if the rank partition between invariant and novelty blocks is mismatched to task similarity, or if Gram statistics are noisy with small per-task data, and it addresses class-incremental vision settings rather than general LLM fine-tuning.
rationale: The method is computationally feasible on constrained infrastructure and has a plausible mechanism, but it targets a specific continual-learning vision workflow, so the reader should validate it on their own task sequence before production adoption.
technique: Bilevel spectral LoRA for continual learning

claims.statement: BISECT replaces null-space-projected (subspace-isolated) LoRA updates in exemplar-free continual learning by splitting a fixed rank-r budget into an invariant carrier from dominant joint Gram-matrix modes and a whitened novelty complement, then folding both into the frozen backbone via a closed-form precision gate. It costs nothing at inference (no extra parameters or FLOPs) and fits a single 24 GB GPU, but adds training-time complexity: Gram-matrix estimation, generalized Rayleigh whitening, and per-task spectral decomposition. It can fail if the spectral-starvation diagnosis does not transfer to the reader's domain, if the rank partition between invariant and novelty blocks is mismatched to task similarity, or if Gram statistics are noisy with small per-task data, and it addresses class-incremental vision settings rather than general LLM fine-tuning.

BISECT outperforms prompt, adapter, and LoRA baselines across eight class-incremental settings on ImageNet-R, ImageNet-A, CIFAR-100, CUB-200, and DomainNet, with zero extra inference parameters or FLOPs; no multiplicative improvement factor is stated in the abstract.
